A log change tells every open view to read the whole map again
why: The signal carries no cards and no events, only the fact that the log grew. Each view then reads the map the same way it reads it on first load. So a view has one way to get the map, and it cannot drift from the log.

To keep every open view in step with the log, the server watches the log. When the log grows, the server sends a bare signal on the live channel to every open page. The signal holds no data. Each page then reads the whole fold again and redraws it (see #pr-log for the fold).

A page never patches its copy of the map from the signal. There is one read path: the full read of the fold. This rule covers the map only. The chat stream carries its own blocks (see #werk-progress).

- The agent adds card #b from the command line.

3. T1 reads the whole fold again. It now shows #a and #b.
4. T2 does the same and shows #a and #b.
